intro: This unit tells a very old story from India. It is called the Ramayana. You will meet Prince Rama and Princess Sita. You will meet brave Hanuman too.
Hindu families have told this story for more than 2,000 years. Many tell it at Diwali. Families in Illinois tell it too.
By the end, you can tell the story in order. You can say what keeping a promise means. You can say why every helper counts.
bigQuestion: What can a story about a promise and helpers teach us?

timeline.t: The king makes a promise to Queen Kaikeyi
Rama, Sita and Lakshmana go to the forest
Sita sees a golden deer, and Rama runs after it
Ravana carries Sita away to Lanka
Rama and Lakshmana meet Hanuman and the monkey army
Hanuman leaps across the sea and finds Sita
Everyone builds a bridge, even a little squirrel
Rama and Sita come home, and people light lamps

words.d: a very old story from India about Prince Rama and Princess Sita
saying you will surely do something
a big place with many trees and animals
something that fools you on purpose
the ten-headed king of Lanka in the Ramayana
Rama's brave helper who leads the monkey army
always staying true to a friend
the Hindu festival of lights in autumn

test.q: Who is the prince in the Ramayana?
test.why: Rama is the prince in the Ramayana.

test.q: Why does Rama go to the forest?
Who goes with Rama to the forest?
test.why: Sita and Lakshmana go with Rama.
The golden deer is a trick to take Rama away.
Ravana, the king of Lanka, takes Sita.
Hanuman leaps across the sea and finds Sita.

test.q: What does the little squirrel teach?
test.why: Rama thanks the tiny squirrel. Every helper counts.

test.q: What do people light when Rama and Sita come home?
test.why: People light lamps to welcome Rama and Sita.

test.q: At which festival do many Hindus remember this story?
test.why: Many Hindus remember Rama and Sita's homecoming at Diwali.

test.q: How do many Hindus honor Rama and Hanuman?
test.why: Many Hindus honor Rama as a form of God and Hanuman as a model of loyal help.

write.prompt: Draw and tell. Pick one helper from the Ramayana: Lakshmana, Hanuman or the little squirrel. Draw how they helped. Tell a grown-up what the story says they did.
tips: Say "The story says..." when you tell it.
Use a word from this unit, like loyal or promise.
